'''Jennifer Taback''' is an American mathematician whose research focuses on [[geometric group theory]] and [[combinatorial group theory]].{{r|wing}} She is the Isaac Henry Wing Professor of Mathematics and Chair of the Mathematics Department at [[Bowdoin College]] in Maine.{{r|profile}}

==Education and career==
After earning a bachelor's degree in mathematics at [[Yale University]] in 1993, Taback went to the [[University of Chicago]] for graduate study in mathematics, earning a master's degree in 1994 and completing her Ph.D. in 1998.{{r|cv}} Her 1998 doctoral dissertation, ''Quasi-Isometric Rigity for <math>PSL_2\bigl(\mathbb{Z}[\tfrac1p]\bigr)</math>'', was supervised by [[Benson Farb]].{{r|mg}}

After a postdoctoral stay at the [[University of California, Berkeley]] as Charles B. Morrey assistant professor, she became an assistant professor of mathematics at the [[University at Albany]] in 1999, moving to her present position at Bowdoin in 2004. She was tenured as an associate professor in 2007, and promoted to full professor in 2012.{{r|cv}}

She was appointed to the Isaac Henry Wing Professorship in 2021; the professorship was endowed in 1906 by a former Bowdoin student.{{r|wing}}

==Recognition==
Taback was elected to the 2026 class of Fellows of the [[American Mathematical Society]].{{r|fams}}
